jobs.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Paralegal role at Global University Systems because the in-house legal context genuinely interests me, and my background in case management, document review, legal research and client-facing advice maps directly onto what the role requires.

At Bryan Cave Leighton Paisner, I spent a year supporting complex disputes across international arbitration and real estate litigation. In arbitration, I reviewed and organised evidence, amended sections of a claimant's memorial, drafted procedural orders and procedural histories, and coordinated documents across an international team under significant deadline pressure. When I became the only junior supporting the team shortly before a major submission, I tracked outstanding actions across multiple workstreams and helped ensure the filing went out on time. That experience gave me a clear picture of what organised, deadline-driven case management actually looks like in practice.

Since July 2026, I have been advising clients at Citizens Advice East Berkshire on welfare, housing, employment and debt matters. Each matter involves taking detailed factual statements, identifying the relevant legal issues, drafting correspondence, preparing document schedules and maintaining confidential case records from instruction through to submission. Translating complex procedural rules into clear, practical guidance for people in difficult circumstances has sharpened my ability to communicate legal issues accessibly, which I expect would be useful in an in-house team dealing with colleagues and stakeholders who are not legally trained.

My academic work is also relevant. I hold a 2:1 LLB from UCL and an LLM in Comparative and International Dispute Resolution from Queen Mary, where I studied legal research, evidence analysis and international procedural law. My dissertation examined data protection law across jurisdictions, and a separate taught module on data privacy and governance received a mark of 75.

GUS operates across multiple jurisdictions and institutions, and the legal team's work will span a wide range of issues touching on regulatory compliance, contracts and institutional governance. That breadth is exactly what I am looking to develop into at paralegal level, building on the foundation I have in research, case management and drafting.

Yours sincerely,
Maria Silva

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Litigation Legal Assistant role in Bexleyheath because litigation support is where my practical experience is strongest, and this role offers the kind of varied caseload exposure that I want to build on at this stage of my career.

My most relevant experience is the year I spent at Bryan Cave Leighton Paisner, where I supported two litigation teams across international arbitration and real estate disputes. In the arbitration rotation, I became the only junior supporting the team shortly before a significant submission deadline. That meant coordinating documents across the matter, tracking outstanding actions and helping ensure everything was filed on time, which is directly comparable to the file and deadline management this role involves. I also maintained structured electronic case files throughout, and liaised with the client about required documents and with an external translator about Romanian-language materials. In the real estate disputes rotation, I prepared electronic hearing bundles, assisted with skeleton arguments, conducted legal research on leasehold and landlord and tenant issues, and handled matter opening and closure using iManage.

At Citizens Advice, I have continued developing the client-facing side of legal support. I take detailed factual statements from clients, prepare correspondence and document schedules, and manage matters from first instruction through to submission while keeping accurate case records. Many of my clients are in difficult circumstances, so translating procedural requirements into plain, practical guidance is a regular part of the work.

I am drawn to this role because a busy litigation department with a varied caseload is the environment where I have consistently learned the most. Working across different matter types at BCLP showed me how quickly exposure to a range of disputes builds both legal understanding and practical confidence, and I want to continue developing in that kind of setting. My LLM in Comparative and International Dispute Resolution, which I am completing this year at Queen Mary, sits alongside that practical background rather than replacing it.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss my application further.

Yours sincerely,
Maria Silva

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Knowledge Paralegal role in A&O Shearman's Global Financial Markets Group. My interest in financial markets work developed from a specific point. At the A&O Shearman open day in August 2026, a session on private equity transactions and a workshop on lender security, including examples involving aircraft and ship financing, gave me a concrete picture of how legal work shapes market practice at the transactional level. I followed that up by completing a Coursera course on private equity, studying fund structures, leverage and exit strategies, because I wanted to understand the commercial mechanics that sit behind the legal documentation. That progression is why a knowledge-focused role in GFM is the right next step for me, not a generic ambition.

My research and writing skills have been tested in contexts that translate directly to knowledge work. At BCLP, across a year-long placement in international arbitration and real estate disputes, I drafted procedural histories, amended sections of a claimant's memorial and prepared procedural orders. I also conducted legal and factual research on easements, leasehold issues and rights of light, writing up findings in a form the fee-earner could use immediately. At Q-Legal, I produced a formal written advice letter on UK GDPR obligations for a data-driven start-up, translating statutory requirements into commercially focused guidance under a solicitor's supervision. Both roles required me to frame legal analysis clearly for a specific audience rather than reproduce the law in the abstract.

Organising and maintaining structured materials under pressure is something I have done consistently. At BCLP I became the sole junior supporting an arbitration team shortly before a significant submission deadline, coordinating documents, tracking outstanding actions and helping ensure on-time filing. At Citizens Advice I now manage matters from instruction to submission, maintaining confidential case records and meeting deadlines across a varied caseload. I understand that knowledge work depends on that same discipline applied to resources and outputs the wider team relies on.

A&O Shearman is where the interest started, and this role is a direct extension of that.

Yours sincerely,
Maria Silva

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the paralegal role at EMG Solicitors in Reading. EMG's focus on Court of Protection, Mental Health Law and Dispute Resolution connects directly with the client-facing and case management work I have been doing at Citizens Advice East Berkshire, where I advise vulnerable clients daily on welfare benefits, housing, employment and debt matters.

At Citizens Advice I manage matters from initial instruction through to submission. That means taking detailed factual statements, identifying evidential gaps, drafting correspondence and applications, and maintaining confidential case records while juggling competing deadlines across an active caseload. Many of my clients are in difficult personal circumstances, so I have had to develop real judgement about how to communicate complex procedural rules clearly and sensitively without losing accuracy. That combination of case administration rigour and client-facing communication is, I think, directly relevant to the kind of work EMG does across its vulnerable-client practice areas.

Before Citizens Advice, I spent a year at Bryan Cave Leighton Paisner as a placement student, split between International Arbitration and Real Estate Disputes. In the arbitration team I coordinated documents, tracked procedural deadlines and helped prepare the Claimant's memorial ahead of a significant submission deadline, at a point when I was the only junior supporting the team. In the disputes team I reviewed documents, prepared electronic hearing bundles and assisted with skeleton arguments and court filings. Both rotations gave me structured experience of managing large volumes of confidential material across several matters at once, which I continued developing through my LLM at Queen Mary, where I completed research on cross-jurisdictional data protection and procedural issues in dispute resolution.

What draws me to EMG specifically is the breadth of its practice alongside that clear focus on genuinely helping clients through difficult situations. My background has developed across several of EMG's core areas, and I want to build on it in a firm where the work is varied and where client outcomes are taken seriously. I am based in Maidenhead and the Reading office is an easy commute, which means I can commit fully from day one.

Yours sincerely,
Maria Silva

jobs.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Junior Legal Secretary role at Birchrose Associates because my background in property disputes and legal document management at BCLP gives me a practical foundation for supporting a busy property team from day one.

During my year at BCLP, I spent six months in the Real Estate Disputes team supporting fee earners across multiple concurrent matters. I prepared electronic hearing bundles, assisted with skeleton arguments and court materials, maintained matter records on iManage, handled court filings and tracked deadlines across competing instructions. Managing large volumes of confidential documents under time pressure while keeping files accurate and organised was a core part of the role, and it is the kind of work I find genuinely satisfying to do well. I received feedback from a partner and associate that my performance was comparable to a newly qualified solicitor, which I think reflected how seriously I took the administrative and document management side of the work, not just the legal research.

Alongside that, my current role at Citizens Advice requires me to manage matters from initial instruction through to submission, drafting correspondence, preparing document schedules and maintaining confidential case records to deadline. Translating complex procedural requirements into clear, practical steps for clients is something I do regularly, including for individuals dealing with housing and debt matters, which has sharpened how I communicate and organise information under pressure.

I am drawn to this role in a property team specifically because property disputes at BCLP was where I saw most clearly how important precise document management and reliable administrative support are to how a matter runs. Fee earners dealing with rights of light, leasehold disputes and landlord and tenant matters depend on that support being accurate and timely. I would bring that understanding, along with direct experience of the tools and workflows, to this position.

Yours sincerely,
Maria Silva

Dear Hiring Manager,

The European Patent Paralegal role at Talentmark's pharmaceutical client in Bracknell is not my usual area of practice, but the core of the work, reviewing incoming documentation, maintaining organised records and tracking procedural deadlines within a regulated, high-stakes environment, maps directly onto what I have been doing across my placements and current role.

At BCLP I spent six months embedded in an international arbitration team, becoming the only junior supporting the team shortly before a major submission deadline. I coordinated documents, tracked outstanding actions across a complex matter and helped ensure on-time filing. Working with large volumes of procedural material under real deadline pressure taught me how to maintain accuracy when the pace picks up. That same discipline carried into my current role at Citizens Advice, where I manage matters from instruction through to submission independently: taking detailed factual statements, identifying evidential gaps, preparing document schedules and maintaining confidential case records across a caseload of welfare, employment and housing matters simultaneously.

I do not have a background in patent law specifically, but I have handled document review and procedural tracking in both litigation and advisory contexts, and I understand how much turns on getting the administrative infrastructure right in regulated proceedings. The pharmaceutical context adds a layer I find genuinely interesting. My LLM dissertation examined data protection development across jurisdictions, which meant spending time with regulatory frameworks and understanding how compliance obligations interact with commercial operations. The European Patent Office's procedural regime is a different body of rules, but the discipline of reading regulatory requirements carefully and translating them into accurate, well-organised case management is one I have practised in several contexts.

The Bracknell location is straightforward for me to reach from Maidenhead, and the hybrid model fits how I currently work. I would welcome the chance to discuss how my experience handling procedural documentation and deadline management could contribute to the team.

Yours sincerely,
Maria Silva

jobs.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Senior Private Client Solicitor position at Gardner Leader. Although this role requires a qualified solicitor, I want to draw your attention to my background in case preparation, client communication and document drafting in case you have paralegal or legal assistant openings within the Private Client team, or in case this application is of use for future recruitment.

My year at Bryan Cave Leighton Paisner gave me direct experience of managing complex matters under pressure. In the Real Estate Disputes team I prepared hearing bundles, maintained matter records on iManage, tracked deadlines across several concurrent files, and supported skeleton arguments and court filings. In the International Arbitration team I took on sole responsibility for coordinating documents and tracking outstanding actions shortly before a major submission deadline, which required both careful organisation and sound judgement about priorities.

At Citizens Advice East Berkshire I now advise clients on welfare benefits, housing, family and debt matters. I take detailed factual statements, draft correspondence and applications, and explain complex procedural rules clearly to people who are often in difficult circumstances. Working with vulnerable clients on sensitive matters has sharpened my ability to communicate carefully and to manage expectations honestly, skills that are central to private client work.

Gardner Leader's Thames Valley base and its reputation for private client work make it a natural fit for where I want to develop. I live in Maidenhead and am familiar with the firm's presence locally. My LLM dissertation examined data protection across jurisdictions, and my LLB included modules in company and commercial law, so I have a grounding in the academic framework that underpins estate planning and related advisory work, even though I have not yet practised in private client directly.

If you do not currently have a suitable opening, I would welcome the chance to be considered for any paralegal vacancy in the Private Client team as it arises.

Yours sincerely,
Maria Silva
